Meta
01Meta · Instagram Shops2020–2023

Which product details make someone buy?

Deciding which information the product page should show, for which product and which shopper.

9 of 17
tested variables drove conversion. Price guarantee was not one of them.
01Problem
  • One product page layout served every category and did little for conversion.
  • Engineering planned an ML "dynamic display" but did not know which variables to model.
02Method
  • 12 in-depth interviews with recent online clothing buyers (5 men, 7 women, aged 20–45).
  • Discrete choice survey, n=9,000 across 5 categories: 8 screens × 3 options, 17 variables, 90 levels.
  • Card sorts on page elements.
03Insight
  • 3 fashion-specific variables and 6 cross-category "value" variables drive more conversion.
  • A price guarantee, assumed to be a strong lever, was not a significantly stronger driver.
04Impact
  • The 9 variables were prioritized in ML model training.
  • A value model now picks what to show per product, per user.
  • Product page redesigned as a personalized dynamic display.
  • Price guarantee feature deprioritized.
02Meta · Express Wi-Fi2020–2023

Why weren't people in Delhi using free Wi-Fi?

Diagnosing a rollout that looked like a failure, to keep a city partnership alive.

+36%
weekly registrations after the fixes
01Problem
  • After successful launches elsewhere, Delhi had far lower usage than forecast.
  • 85% of users were men aged 18–36. Data could not explain why.
  • The City of Delhi partnership depended on proving value.
02Method
  • In-depth interviews with users and non-users.
  • Platform data: phone type, data use, speed, by gender.
  • Satellite mapping of the busiest access points.
03Insight
  • Registration asked for private national ID details and documents many people did not have.
  • Literacy made the form hard, especially on feature phones.
  • The network served the street. Men went out to use it; women were less likely to, for safety and cultural reasons.
04Impact
  • Partner agreed to simplify registration.
  • Sign in with Facebook added for some users.
  • Form redesigned around icons.
  • Access points reconfigured toward residential areas.
  • Weekly registrations +36%.
SodaStream · PepsiCo
03SodaStream · PepsiCo2017–2020

Why do people stop refilling?

Finding the real cause of churn in a business that depends on repeat cylinder swaps.

2 factories
built to produce the redesigned cylinder system
01Problem
  • High churn. Revenue depends on people replacing gas cylinders often.
  • Several earlier efforts had not found actionable drivers.
02Method
  • In-home ethnography: watching how people chill, store, use and refill.
  • Part of a global qual and quant program across 45 markets.
03Insight
  • People want water cold, so they need 2–3 bottles chilling. Machines shipped with 1.
  • The habit takes 2–3 refills to form. Machines shipped with 1 cylinder.
  • Empties were forgotten in car trunks.
  • Gas felt like a commodity; loyalty was low.
04Impact
  • Patented quick-connect cylinder mechanism and a new patented valve.
  • New machine built around them, and 2 new factories.
  • Pink cylinder for brand recognition; multi-bottle sets.
  • Home-delivery subscription extended to more markets.
Microsoft Copilot Studio
04Microsoft · Copilot Studio2025–2026

How do teams decide an AI agent is ready to ship?

Defining what an agent evaluation product must do, for no-code, low-code and pro-code builders.

35
builders interviewed across two studies, plus 170+ jobs to be done
01Problem
  • Agents were entering business-critical work faster than teams could check them.
  • The product team needed to know what to build first and how to structure testing, evaluation and monitoring.
02Method
  • 19 interviews with builders using our product and competing tools.
  • 16 interviews split by low-code / pro-code and user / non-user, coded with a shared codebook.
  • Competitive IA analysis; 170+ jobs to be done in 11 themes.
03Insight
  • "What broke?" (debugging) and "Is this acceptable?" (evaluation) are different jobs owned by different people.
  • Release decisions were made by consensus, not metrics.
  • Many failures could not be reproduced once models or tools drifted.
04Impact
  • Defined the agent evaluation controls.
  • Workflow trace views prioritized on the roadmap for debugging.
  • Quality and safety criteria adopted by product, security and governance teams.
  • Shipped as an interactive JTBD simulator for PMs.
05Microsoft · Copilot Studio2025–2026

Can builders understand an AI evaluation result?

Rapid usability rounds on agent evaluation and safety evaluation flows.

4 countries
recruited in days with my own study automation
01Problem
  • Evaluation features shipped faster than traditional studies could run.
  • The team needed evidence on each iteration within days.
02Method
  • Unmoderated test, 12 builders, 2 prototypes of the same task.
  • Think-aloud test, 8 low-code builders in 4 countries, scored against a usability rulebook.
03Insight
  • Everyone could start an evaluation; most stalled at the results. They saw pass/fail but not why, or what to do.
  • Switching views re-ran the model, adding compute cost.
  • Without severity levels, people escalated every failure.
04Impact
  • Prioritized fix list: visible pass/fail, severity and baselines, re-run only failed prompts, results beside configuration, handoff.
  • Framing friction as compute cost brought engineering on board.
  • Rapid-test template adopted by the team.
06Microsoft · Copilot Studio2025

What do builders need to own security for AI agents?

Security work is moving from security teams to the people who build agents.

10 hours
of interviews with developers new to security work
01Problem
  • Developers without security training were being asked to catch risks early.
  • The product needed to flag issues without slowing them down.
02Method
  • 10 × 60-minute interviews, customers and non-customers.
  • Evaluation of design drafts with participants.
  • Synthesis of 6 internal studies and 13 external papers.
03Insight
  • Builders think in threat levels (critical to low), not protection levels.
  • They confused real-time and historical status on dashboards.
  • They learned of threats by email, often days late.
04Impact
  • Recommendations: threat-based severity, a clear real-time vs. historical split, a shared workspace for security teams and builders, all permissions editable in the UI.

★ UserTesting ILLUMI Award 2026

AI-first study automation

Problem: setting up unmoderated studies by hand was slow and error-prone.

  • A conversational agent sets up a full UserTesting study from a short brief.
  • An MCP server connects the assistant to the UserTesting API; browser automation covers steps the API cannot.
  • Teammates request access through a self-serve flow.

Impact: Microsoft named winner of UserTesting's 2026 Innovation Catalyst Award; individual ILLUMI Award.

Demo: Annotated highlights: from a short conversation to a configured UserTesting study with screener logic, task instructions and launch.Watch the highlights and the full 10-minute run at jordanayoung-mod.github.io/Jordana-Young-Portfolio
Hackathon 2026

Human Value Add Assessor

Problem: teams need a fair way to show what a person adds beyond what AI produces.

Walkthrough (1:53): upload → artifact type → rules → score with cited evidence.

  • Upload a deck, doc, sheet or page. One model writes the brief, a second makes a blind AI version, a third compares.
  • 98-attribute rubric in 8 categories.
  • Every score needs cited evidence; the creator's identity is hidden.
Framework + live scorer

Human Grade Benchmark Kit

Problem: "consumer-grade" was a goal with no definition.

  • 25 rules from teardowns of 30 consumer apps and 15 creation tools, including 7 neuroinclusion rules.
  • A plugin walks a product in a real browser, screenshots each step and scores it.
  • Piloted on our own product.
Evidence

Signal Atlas

Answers a product question with evidence from research, customer calls and telemetry. Runs a counter-evidence check every time.

Talk · IIEX West 2026 · San Francisco · October 2026

From Hype to Human

A New Horizon for AI and Business. Co-presented with Space Doctors. AI efficiency gets business to a frontier, but no further. Moving past it means questioning the assumptions AI is being added to.

AssumptionWith AIWhat if…
Junior staff learn by doing simpler tasks.AI absorbs first drafts and routine analysis, so juniors lose practice.Junior work were designed for learning?
Consensus produces better decisions.Similar AI tools push teams toward similar, safe answers.AI exposed disagreement, and people made the distinctive calls?
Creativity is valuable in every role.Idea volume can be mistaken for originality.Creativity were judged by framing and selection, not volume?

Microsoft · 2025–2026

The Future of Enterprise

Method: semiotic analysis with an external agency, leader interviews, competitor decoding.

Insight: three cultural shifts in what workers will value.

Impact: UXR Days 2026 talk; basis for a 4-day leadership workshop and a 3-day design sprint I co-led.

Essay · 2026

The Convergence Trap

Default AI use pulls teams toward the same average answers. I argue for using AI heavily where work converges and holding it back where ideas need to diverge.

Editorial · 2026

Neuroinclusion in enterprise AI

At least 1 in 5 employees is neurodivergent and about a third never disclose it, so opt-in modes miss most of them. Output: an 8-principle audit used in product assessments.

Also: a recurring STEEP trend-scanning program for the product organization (minimum three independent sources per trend), and a POV on a three-layer model of agent trust: response quality, workflow reliability, governance.
